metadata.title: Coinbase Stock Jumped 12% Yesterday. Bitcoin’s Breakout Wasn’t the Whole Story.

content.text:
Key Takeaways
-
Bitcoin Breakout: Coinbase stock jumped 12% on Friday, September 18, closing at $194, as bitcoin cleared $80,941 and new CFTC and SEC rulemaking reignited the regulatory tailwind Congress couldn't deliver.
-
Buy Wall: TIKR tracks 18 buys, 3 outperforms, and 11 holds on Coinbase stock.
-
Target Slide: The mean target has fallen every quarter since peaking near $376 last September, now sitting at $202, even as buy ratings climbed from 13 to 18 analysts over the same year.
Why Coinbase Stock Jumped 12% as Bitcoin Cleared $80,000
Coinbase (COIN) stock jumped 12% on Friday, September 18, closing at $194, as bitcoin's rally past $80,000 met a fresh round of crypto rulemaking that erased the week's earlier losses. Bitcoin gained 5.7% to $80,941, ether rose 5.9% to $2,594, and the broader crypto sector caught a bid that lifted Robinhood 9% and Strategy nearly 13% alongside Coinbase stock.
The bounce arrived days after the U.S. Senate blocked the Clarity Act on September 15, a defeat that had knocked Coinbase stock down as much as 9% and dragged bitcoin toward $76,000. Regulators didn't wait for Congress. The SEC had unveiled a five-year exemption for tokenized stock trading just a day earlier, and the CFTC followed Friday with proposed rules for crypto asset markets plus a new category letting software providers route users into prediction markets without broker registration.
"We are so pleased with Chair Atkins and Chair Sealig's approach to rulemaking, innovation, really being deep in the process and driving forward their own regulatory clarity agendas," Coinbase CFO Alesia Haas told analysts at Citi's Global TMT Conference on September 10, addressing the risk that a stalled Senate vote might leave the industry without a legislative path. Eight days later, that's exactly the route regulators took.
The CFTC's prediction market rule lands on Coinbase's fastest-growing product. Prediction markets crossed $100 million in annualized revenue within months of launch and grew 106% quarter over quarter in the second quarter, Haas said. Clearer rules around that business, plus the tokenized equities Coinbase already began offering non-U.S. customers, gave the company's "Everything Exchange" pitch a regulatory floor that one Senate vote couldn't provide.
Bitcoin's climb back above $80,000 didn't just lift sentiment for a day. It repriced Coinbase stock for a regulatory path that no longer runs through one vote in Washington.
